extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing AMS monographs (mathematicians preparing LaTeX source for AMS publication)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting LaTeX source, figures, bibliographies, indexes, and permissions for AMS monographs; aimed at authors producing publication-quality manuscripts using AMS classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareMathOperator for new operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \DeclareMathOperator to add additional operator names (see [AMG, §5]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines functions and operators like log and lim consistently; follow AMS-LATEX recommendations for operator names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference citation style and commands
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of reference citations, though publication-dependent, is usually roman; always use the standard LaTeX \cite command when citing a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate forms are provided by natbib for author-year style. For internal references use \ref (may need upref to force roman in non-roman environments). Use \eqref for numbered equation references to include parentheses and produce roman type (e.g., \eqref{eqn2.4}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises environments (xca and xcb)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the xca environment for exercises that appear individually within a section; the xcb environment is defined only for monographs for exercises at the end of a chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define xca in the preamble with \theoremstyle{definition} and \newtheorem; xcb is presented as a section and often formatted as an enumerated list with \item for each exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: include index terms in TeX and use MakeIndex
rubrics_metrics.description: Index terms should be included directly in the TeX file(s) and the output from TeX should conform to the rules of MakeIndex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run MakeIndex separately from LaTeX and rerun LaTeX to incorporate indexes. Do not include the makeidx package (AMS classes include needed tags); put \makeindex in the preamble and \printindex where the index should appear. For multiple indexes, use the imakeidx package with its [original] option to preserve AMS formatting; specify additional indexes in the preamble and use appropriate \index[...] and \printindex[...] commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Floats should be numbered consistently and placed to avoid pagination problems: be placed at top or bottom of the page, have an in-text reference, and appear within the same section as their first text reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A figure or table should not precede its first text reference unless both appear on the same page spread. Allow figures and tables to float according to LaTeX defaults; avoid forcing placement with options like [h!] which can introduce production problems. For electronic manuscripts, final placement is determined by AMS production staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions: position and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions for floating inserts are usually positioned above a table and below a figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General structure: use \begin{figure} or \begin{table}, include file/code, then \caption{caption text} and a \label{reference label} (label usually given after the caption). Caption text may be omitted if none is desired. Caption heading numbering is supplied automatically. Avoid caption packages whose style may not match AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering not required for floats
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS classes center the content of table and figure environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \centering or a center environment inside figure/table; it's unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography package support
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographies may be prepared using either amsrefs or BibTEX; methods using other packages, including biblatex, are not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsrefs or BibTEX to produce .bbl files in the form appropriate for AMS publications; these are the recommended methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced references (MathSciNet integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: References in monographs will be replaced by enhanced information from MathSciNet when available, in amsrefs format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced references can add DOIs, links to MathSciNet and AMS journals; if an entry is not present, styles may be updated for consistency. Report errors (e.g., incorrect MR numbers) to eprod-support@ams.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using BibTEX with AMS: styles and chapter bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: Two BibTEX styles are provided: amsplain.bst (numeric labels; preferred for articles) and amsalpha.bst (labels from author and year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include \bibliographystyle{...} and \bibliography{...} in the file. For chapter-specific bibliographies, after BibTEX processing insert the .bbl contents into the chapter .tex and change the environment name to inchapterbibliography so it appears as a section rather than a chapter. BibTEX will sort items and may alter order depending on style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natbib
rubrics_metrics.description: The natbib package provides an author-year style compatible with AMS document classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily use natbib only for monographs on historical topics (author-year style); be aware of compatibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsrefs package usage and interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: amsrefs is a LaTeX package for preparing structured bibliographies and can be used instead of BibTEX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three ways to use amsrefs: (1) enter items directly with biblist and \bib, (2) import from .ltb, (3) import from .bib via BibTEX and special styles. When using amsrefs with BibTEX, load \usepackage{amsrefs} (after hyperref). There is no need for a \bibliographystyle command with amsrefs; such commands are ignored because amsrefs invokes the correct style automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a bibliography without a package
rubrics_metrics.description: You may prepare references using the thebibliography environment: \begin{thebibliography}{model label} ... \end{thebibliography}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This environment becomes an unnumbered chapter in a monograph (use inchapterbibliography for chapter-specific lists). Use the widest label as the model in the \begin command (e.g., 99 for two-digit numeric labels). Begin each item with \bibitem{bibitem label} and optionally provide a printed label in square brackets, e.g., \bibitem[ABC]{Arno1994}. The printed label must not include math or special characters; use \bysame for repeated authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for third-party material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must obtain permission for the use of any material (graphics, photographs, text) from other sources and should use the Society’s Permission Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions must be obtained for both print and electronic rights for all editions (present and future) and must be free of any restrictions that limit AMS's ability to produce, publish, promote, and distribute the Work in any territory, language, or medium. If applying via a publisher's form, match AMS requirements closely. Permissions with restrictions may lead to omission of material. Send written permission to AMS along with the final manuscript. Contact acquisitions@ams.org for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: use standard inclusion package and basic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a standard TeX graphics inclusion macro package (recommended: graphicx); do not place graphics in subdirectories; number figures consistently; include in-text references; set figure captions in TeX; set figure captions below the figure; ensure correct sizing and that figures do not extend into margins; ensure overlaid labels do not extend beyond allotted figure space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figure code is extensive (15-20 lines or more), place in a dedicated file and \input it. Avoid overlay labels extending into margins; check final positioning. For electronic manuscripts, AMS production staff will determine final placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic file formats by series
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred file formats vary by series: for AMS Books the preferred format is EPS; for AMS/MAA Press Books, STM Library, and Pure & Applied Undergraduate Texts the preferred format is PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow series-specific preferred formats for best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution requirements for bitmap graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Required resolutions at 100%: line art 600 ppi; halftone 300 ppi; combination halftone 600 ppi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet these minimums at the actual size to be printed; insufficient resolution can cause poor reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create graphics at 100% print size; do not resize in TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Create graphics at 100% of the size at which they will be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure is too large, resize in a graphics program rather than in TeX. Applies also to photographs (do not scale photographs in TeX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic file naming
rubrics_metrics.description: File names should be no longer than 20 alphanumeric characters; do not use accented characters; avoid overly generic names such as fig01.eps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, descriptive alphanumeric names to avoid file handling issues in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines and rule weights in graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use a line/rule weight less than half a point (.5 point) at 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scaling, compensate by increasing line weights (.5 pt, 1 pt, 1.5 pt increments recommended). Gray or colored lines should have at least 1 pt at 100%; lighter weights can disappear or look jagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shades of gray (screen) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Screens (dot patterns simulating gray) should be between 10% and 85% density.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen density increments should be no less than 10%; do not put (black or colored) type on a screen darker than 35% (type becomes illegible). White type may be used only on 100% black; avoid white type on gray backgrounds which looks broken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts in graphics: embedding and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Fonts used in graphics should match those used in text and should be fully embedded in graphics; use Type 1 outline fonts rather than bitmap fonts; do not subset fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to embed, convert fonts to paths/outlines before exporting to EPS. Subsetting can cause font errors and missing characters. Avoid fonts named for cities (Chicago, Monaco, Geneva, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-part figures: assemble outside TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-part figures should be configured as one figure in a graphics program, not in TeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning multiple parts is easier and more cost-effective in a graphics program than in TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cropping and bounding boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not crop by pasting areas of white over portions of the graphic; clip or crop within the graphics application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pasting white makes bounding boxes larger and causes inclusion problems. Verify bounding box information to avoid unexpected clipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics: color spaces and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand RGB (screen) and CMYK (printing) color spaces and gamuts; submit graphics intended for print in CMYK format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RGB files will be converted to CMYK (AMS cannot guarantee matching); colors viewed on monitors or home printers will not match press output. AMS optimizes color graphics for print; consult Graphics group if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics for black-and-white printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Color graphics to be printed in black-and-white or grayscale should be converted to grayscale before submission and checked for legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some colors (e.g., yellow) may disappear or map to similar tones; check output on a black-and-white printer to ensure elements remain distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colored lines and tints
rubrics_metrics.description: Colored lines should be no less than .5 point in width; colored lines in inherently light colors (e.g., yellow, cyan) should be at or near 100% tint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Light tinted lines at small widths may be invisible or broken in print; use thicker lines and high tints for light colors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type within graphics: size and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic type size within graphics should be no less than 10 point at 100%; do not put type on a dark background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10-point is acceptable for print but may be small on-screen (72 ppi). Check black-and-white printouts for legibility. Avoid dark-on-dark color combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables are a special kind of graphic and must not exceed the width of the text block; very wide tables can be rotated with the rotating package and sidewaystable environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set table captions above the table. When rotating, ensure the left-hand side after rotation is at the bottom of the page. Consult [MG, chapter 5] and [voss-tbl] for further formatting help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs must be at minimum 300 dpi at the actual size to be printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File formats allowed include EPS, TIFF, or JPEG. Color photographs must be saved in CMYK format. Do not scale photographs in TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX-native graphics packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Several TeX coding methods are acceptable for graphics: tikz (PGF), pstricks, xy/xypic, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tikz works with dvips, pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX, LuaLaTeX; pstricks is most easily used with dvips-based TeX (with care for pdfLaTeX). See package documentation and references ([tkz], [voss-pst], [GM]) for detailed usage and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using labeling packages for graphics: check overflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages that apply labels to graphics can ensure consistent fonts, but labels do not modify graphic dimensions and may extend outside the graphic boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check for labels extending into margins or overprinting surrounding material; if labels cannot be positioned within boundaries, add extra space (e.g., with \vspace) to compensate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission: send only necessary source files and exact accepted files
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, send the source file(s) to the AMS office, including TeX source and graphics files; send only the files needed to process or archive the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files must be the EXACT files used to generate the copy accepted for publication (do not send .log or .aux unless needed). If multiple files, bundle into a single compressed archive (Zip recommended) to reduce name conflicts. Use www.ams.org/submit-book-journal (web server preferred; requires AMS web account) or email pub-submit@ams.org with attachments; include publication code and author names in the subject line to speed processing. If difficulties arise, contact AMS Technical Support or acquisitions as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS technical and TeX support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS provides technical support contacts and points authors to TeX resources and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Publications Technical Group (tech-support@ams.org) or Acquisitions (acquisitions@ams.org) for submission problems. AMS TeX pages (www.ams.org/tex) link to CTAN and distributions. For community assistance, consult comp.text.tex (groups.google.com/forum/comp.text.tex) and tex.stackexchange.com; read package documentation and AMS User Guides. Updates for amsmath from CTAN; amscls from CTAN or AMS server.
